result:
Both key files confirm the agent's report exactly. Here's the full path from silent overdue issue to a single, targeted alert.

## What starts the check

Two entry points converge on the same job, so the sweep can be triggered either externally or internally:

- **`src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts`** — a `POST` handler meant to be hit by an external scheduler (e.g. Vercel Cron). It validates a shared secret via `assertCronSecret(request)` and then calls `runOverdueIssueJob(new Date())`.
- **`src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`** — an in-process fallback. `startScheduler()` (kicked off once from `src/instrumentation.ts::register()` at process boot) sets a one-minute `setInterval` calling `tick(now)`. `tick()` checks `isDue("overdue-issues", now)` against an hourly cadence (`CADENCE_MINUTES["overdue-issues"] = 60`), and when due, calls `queue.ts::enqueue(...)` then `drain()`, whose `runHandler` dynamically imports and calls the same `runOverdueIssueJob`.

Either way, execution lands in `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts::runOverdueIssueJob(now)`.

## Narrowing the set of issues that count

Inside that job, for each org (paged via `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup(ORG_BATCH=50)`), it calls **`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts::listOverdueIssues(orgId, now)`**. The query combines: org scoping, `livePredicate(issues.archivedAt, {})` (excludes archived issues), `isNotNull(issues.dueAt)` (must actually have a due date), `lt(issues.dueAt, now)` (the due date has passed), and `inArray(issues.status, ["backlog","todo","in_progress","in_review"])` — i.e. everything except the closed statuses `done`/`canceled`.

## What the checker does and doesn't own

`runOverdueIssueJob` is explicitly a **detector, not a notifier** — its own comment states it "owns no notification logic: it announces the fact, and whoever cares... reacts on the bus." For each qualifying issue it calls `emit("issue.overdue", payload)` from `src/lib/event-bus.ts`, a typed in-process pub/sub, passing along `orgId`, `issueId`, `dueAt`, and `assigneeId`. It never touches the notifications table or any channel directly — that's delegated entirely to whoever subscribes to the event.

## Stopping repeat announcements

There's no DB column for this (no `notifiedAt`/`lastNotifiedAt` field exists in the schema). Instead, dedup is a plain in-memory `Set<string>` named `reported`, module-scoped in `overdue-issue-job.ts`. Before emitting, the loop checks `if (reported.has(issue.id)) continue;`, and adds the id right after a successful emit. This means an issue is announced once per process lifetime — a still-overdue issue is never re-emitted on later sweeps, but a process restart would reset the set and re-announce everything still overdue. (`resetOverdueTracking()` exists solely so tests can clear it between scenarios.)

## Reaching the one assignee via their chosen channels

The event is picked up in **`src/server/services/notification-service.ts`**, wired at module load via `registerFanOut()` (loaded transitively when `event-registry.ts` is imported at boot). Its `issue.overdue` subscriber first checks `payload.assigneeId === null` — this is the point where "one specific person" is selected; unassigned issues never notify anyone. It then calls the shared dispatcher `notify(orgId, "issue_overdue", [assigneeId], payload)`.

`notify()`:
1. Looks up the assignee's stored preference via `notification-preference-repository.ts::getPreference(orgId, recipientId, "issue_overdue")`.
2. Runs it through `resolveChannels(preference, flags)`, which turns the preference into the concrete channel list — `in_app` if enabled, `email` if enabled (and not `digestOnly`-suppressed unless the `digest_email` flag is on). A `null` preference defaults to `["in_app", "email"]`; a fully-muted user is skipped and gets no row at all.
3. Persists one row (with its `channels` array) via `notification-repository.ts::insertNotifications`.

Delivery itself is realized differently per channel: `in_app` is the row itself, surfaced through `listNotifications`/`countUnread` to the dashboard bell/inbox. `email` is not sent immediately from this path — it's only actually dispatched later, in batch, by the separate daily `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts::runDigestEmailJob`, which calls `email-service.ts::sendEmail` for users who opted into `digestOnly`. So an assignee with `email: true, digestOnly: false` gets a row tagged for email but, as currently wired, no job actually sends it — only digest subscribers get a real send.
